title: On to the Final Act
coreMove: Let death be a filter, not theater: place a plain reminder where choices start, then spend the day on speech, work, love, and refusal you can stand behind.

exampleSpecs.audience: learners who think death reminders sound gloomy
exampleSpecs.stakes: confusion could turn a practical filter into a morbid slogan
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Carmen uses memento mori practice to answer a learner's confusion about memento mori.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose reminders stay hidden from the moment of choice
exampleSpecs.stakes: a meaningful object becomes decoration unless it interrupts a habit
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The same reminder changes behavior when moved into the place of choice.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers whose practices stay beautiful but detached from action
exampleSpecs.stakes: mortality may remain a symbol while a neglected duty waits
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Two people use a memento mori note to move from a beautiful practice to one call.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who use calm language to avoid a needed repair
exampleSpecs.stakes: a private practice can become a hiding place for fear
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Madelyn thinks through the wrong turns before using memento mori as a filter for an apology.

exampleSpecs.audience: people ranking time by regret rather than noise
exampleSpecs.stakes: the week may satisfy urgent errands while neglecting the duty that death makes plain
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: The protagonist chooses between the loud errands and the duty she would most regret neglecting.

exampleSpecs.domain: hospital hallway before a family visit
exampleSpecs.audience: readers caught between duty and love when both carry cost
exampleSpecs.stakes: one choice risks work damage, the other risks a final chance with Jude
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Olivia faces two bad options and uses memento mori to choose the cost she can stand behind.
